Job Description:

Data Governance Analyst

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The CMM program is an initiative to support the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AO) in developing a modern cloud-based solution to support all 204+ federal courts across the United States.

GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career. The Data Governance Analyst will be part of the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team responsible for delivering an integrated data governance, engineering, data platform, reporting, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities that support operational decision-making and fulfill AO's data and analytics objectives in support of the CMM program.

The successful candidate will be responsible for establishing, implementing, and maintaining the organization's data governance framework so that data is managed and protected as a strategic enterprise asset and to accelerate CMM modernization efforts. This role acts as a Data Standards Architect, defining and documenting data standards, definitions, and structures across systems, and works closely with legal, compliance, security, and business stakeholders to ensure data is handled in accordance with privacy, security, retention, classification, and regulatory requirements. This role also ensures alignment with Judiciary policies, practices, and the current Data Governance Roadmap, and fosters a data driven culture across the AO and local courts.

The Data Governance Analyst will execute the following responsibilities:

  • Support the development, implementation, and maintenance of the CMM Data Governance framework, policies, standards, procedures, and operating models.
  • Serve as a Data Standards Architect, define, document, and maintain data standards, naming conventions, data definitions, data structures, reference data, and governance requirements.
  • Develop and maintain data governance standards aligned with enterprise architecture, security, privacy, records management, and regulatory requirements.
  • Establish and maintain data ownership, stewardship, accountability, and decision-rights models.
  • Partner with Data Stewards, Data Owners, business stakeholders, security, privacy, legal, records management, and technology teams to operationalize governance requirements.
  • Ensure data assets are appropriately classified and managed based on sensitivity, criticality, and business value.
  • Support compliance with data privacy, security, retention, classification, records management, and regulatory requirements.
  • Translate policies and regulatory requirements into actionable data governance controls and procedures.
  • Identify governance gaps, risks, and areas of non-compliance and coordinate remediation activities.
  • Support data access, sharing, usage, and lifecycle governance processes.
  • Participate in governance councils, working groups, and data domain forums.
  • Develop governance documentation, standards, procedures, decision logs, and supporting artifacts.
  • Monitor adoption and effectiveness of governance policies and standards.
  • Support governance-related assessments, audits, and compliance reviews.
  • Contribute to the development of data governance roadmaps, maturity assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Support the data stewardship program by defining data ownership roles, responsibilities, and RACI models across business and technical teams.
  • Develop training materials and deliver awareness sessions on data governance policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Track, analyze, and report data governance program metrics, maturity, and compliance status to leadership and governance councils.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • MA/MS degree with 5+ years of general experience in information systems and 7+ years of specialized experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in supporting enterprise data governance programs.
  • Experience translating governance policy into practical operational processes in delivery environments.
  • Strong understanding of data quality management, metadata practices, and stewardship models.
  • Experience governing high-sensitivity or regulated data with clear compliance expectations.
  • Experience with data quality profiling and monitoring techniques and common tooling patterns.
  • Experience defining and governing enterprise data standards across multiple teams and delivery pods.
  • Strong background in data modeling, integration patterns, and change data capture concepts.
  • Experience with metadata and catalog tools such as Collibra, Alation, or Qlik.
  • Practical experience implementing glossary and lineage capabilities in modern data platforms.
  • Ability to translate technical metadata into business-friendly definitions and documentation.
  • Experience implementing data privacy controls in regulated or high-sensitivity environments.
  • Experience with access management and operationalizing privacy requirements.
  • Experience partnering with security, governance, and engineering teams to implement compliant data sharing.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in Federal Government or regulated environments.
  • Experience with enterprise data governance frameworks and operating models.
  • Data management certification.

raw.excerpt: At Shakepay, we’re on a mission to usher in the Bitcoin golden age.
raw.description:
At Shakepay, we’re on a mission to usher in the Bitcoin golden age. We’re reimagining financial services to give every Canadian their fair shake.

Our culture is built around doing work that matters, winning as a team, and celebrating success. If you're the kind of person who values growth, shipping fast, and sharing your ideas openly with a group of like-minded people, come and build with us!

About Shakepay

Since 2015, we've been on a mission to help Canadians build long-term wealth through bitcoin. Over the past few years, we've expanded beyond buying and selling bitcoin to offer a growing suite of everyday financial products - including the Shakepay Card, direct deposit, bill payments and Interac e-Transfer - making it easier to earn, save and use bitcoin every day. Today, more than 1.5 million Canadians use Shakepay to grow their bitcoin savings and take control of their financial future as we continue to push the boundaries of what modern financial services can look like.

We’re regulated as an investment dealer across all Canadian provinces and territories, and backed by renowned venture capitalists with a funding of $44M. We have a passionate, loyal, and growing community, and we’re looking for people who want to help us build something truly special.

About the team

The Legal team sits at the center of some of Shakepay’s most important decisions. We partner closely with Product, Compliance, Operations, Finance, People, and leadership to bring new products to market, navigate complex regulatory questions and help the business move quickly with confidence. We believe ownership over hierarchy, practical judgment over perfection, and using technology and AI to rethink how legal work gets done.

About the role

As Senior Legal Counsel, you’ll help shape how millions of Canadians interact with money. You’ll work alongside product, compliance and executive leadership to solve novel legal questions at the intersection of crypto, payments and financial regulation. This is a hands-on role for someone who can navigate ambiguity, provide practical recommendations and wants to help build - not just protect - the business.

What you’ll be doing

  • Partner with Product, Compliance and business teams to help design and launch new products, translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical solutions.
  • Advise on a broad range of legal and regulatory matters across securities, AML/ATF, payments, consumer protection and other areas impacting Shakepay's business.
  • Lead regulatory initiatives, including supporting examinations, audits, licensing work, policy development and engagement with regulators.
  • Provide practical, business-oriented advice to leaders across the company, helping teams navigate ambiguity and make informed decisions while balancing legal, regulatory and operational considerations.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation and scalable processes to improve how legal work gets done and enable the business to move faster.
  • Support the team on a variety of other legal matters as needed, including commercial agreements, corporate governance, employment and strategic projects.

Who we’re looking for

  • Canadian-qualified lawyer with 5+ years of experience, ideally in fintech, payments, financial services, crypto, or a fast-moving technology company.
  • Able to operate independently in a lean team, make decisions with incomplete information, and move work forward without heavy oversight.
  • Business-oriented legal judgment: you start from the product or business outcome, then help the team understand risk, options, and a recommended path.
  • Comfortable advising product and operational teams directly, including on ambiguous questions where there may not be a perfect answer.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex legal issues into clear, practical guidance for non-legal stakeholders.

Bonus points

  • Experience working across both a law firm and an in-house legal team.
  • Experience in a startup or scaleup environment where priorities change quickly and legal support needs to be pragmatic.
  • Familiarity with Bitcoin, crypto, securities, payments, AML, or regulated financial products in Canada.
  • Experience using AI, automation, or lightweight tooling to improve legal work product and team efficiency.

Why join us?

  • Help shape the future of money: Be part of a team that's revolutionizing financial services in Canada, one sat at a time.
  • Impact millions: As cryptocurrency continues to gain traction, our potential for growth is massive. You can help us bring Shakepay and Bitcoin to all Canadians.
  • Grow your career: We’re growing, and so can you! We have programs in place to encourage continuous learning, growth, and development.
  • Ideas, not titles: We want the best ideas to make their way through, no matter where they come from.

Perks and benefits

  • 🤝 Be an owner: Every employee has stock options as part of their total compensation.
  • 🥅 Reach your goals: Develop with continuous feedback and quarterly performance and compensation review.
  • 🦷 Health & wellness: Access to health and dental coverage, including health and wellness spending accounts.
  • 🌎 Remote-friendly: Work from anywhere in Canada, with optional access to our office spaces in Montreal and Toronto.
  • 🆙 Level Up: A $2,000 annual budget for courses, certifications, and training to support your career growth.
  • 🌴 Time off: 20 days of vacation per year. And if you use all your vacation, we give you a $1,000 bonus.
  • 🐣 Parental leave: Enjoy a parental leave top up to 100% of your salary for 18 weeks.
  • 🙌 Have fun together: quarterly team-specific or company-wide offsite to connect with each other.

The base salary may vary based on factors such as years of experience, skills and qualifications. Additionally, employees are eligible for equity, pay increases based on performance, benefits including health and dental care, and paid time off.

We understand that potential can be just as valuable as experience. If you're eager to learn, grow, and contribute to the mission but worry that you may not have the “right” experience, we still want you to apply. We encourage applications from everyone, regardless of background and life experience. We’re firm believers that a little bit of slope makes up for a lot of y-intercept.

We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support certain parts of our hiring process. This can include tools that assist with scheduling, application review, candidate communications, and generating interview notes, guides, or summaries so our team can stay focused on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.

Fluency in English is required due to the percentage of English-speaking customers and the nature of our platform, which is available to all Canadians.

Account Executive, DOJ-Department of Justice

About Trilogy Innovations

At Trilogy Innovations, we are committed to driving meaningful change for our customers and communities through smart, innovative technology that solves real problems. As a growing systems and software engineering company, we partner across public and private sectors to modernize enterprise systems, strengthen security, and deliver high value solutions. We are scaling with purpose, investing in our people, processes, and platforms as we expand. We work hard, think creatively, and value every perspective as we push boundaries and build systems that matter.

Who you are

The Account Executive, Department of Justice is a quota-carrying federal sales professional responsible for driving new business and expanding Trilogy Innovations’ footprint across DOJ agencies and components. Your primary focus is the Department of Justice – including the FBI, DEA, ATF, BOP, USMS, EOIR, OJP, and DOJ headquarters – and you may flex to adjacent federal customers as pipeline priorities evolve. You are the face of Trilogy to DOJ stakeholders, translating mission-critical needs into technology solutions while navigating the full federal acquisition lifecycle. You bring established DOJ relationships, a track record of closing multi-year federal contract awards, and the discipline to manage a complex, long-cycle pipeline.

The anchor portfolio is the Department of Justice (FBI, DEA, ATF, BOP, USMS, EOIR, OJP, NSD, and DOJ headquarters components). The role may flex to adjacent federal civilian customers as the Director, Federal Business Development assigns based on pipeline coverage and strategic priorities. Carries an annual revenue quota with commission structured under the Trilogy Standard BD Commission Plan. Reports directly to the Director, Federal Business Development and serves as Trilogy’s primary point of contact on assigned DOJ customer and partner engagements.

What you will do:

  • Own end-to-end business development strategy and execution for the DOJ portfolio – covering market analysis, account planning, opportunity qualification, capture, proposal, and close.

  • Build and maintain trusted, senior-level relationships with DOJ customers including program managers, contracting officers, and agency decision-makers across FBI, DEA, ATF, BOP, USMS, OJP, EOIR, NSD, and DOJ headquarters.

  • Partner with channel partners, prime integrators and contract vehicle holders to position Trilogy solutions and accelerate deal closure.

  • Lead capture for DOJ pursuits including teaming strategy, win-theme development, pricing-to-win, and B&P investment recommendations to the Director of Federal Business Development.

  • Manage the full sales cycle from prospecting through contract award, including RFI/RFP responses and oral presentations.

  • Maintain an accurate, forecast-ready pipeline in the company CRM; deliver weekly pipeline updates, monthly forecasts, and quarterly business reviews to the leadership team.

  • Partner with Trilogy delivery, solutions, contracts, and finance teams to develop responsive technical and cost proposals, Statements of Work, and Bills of Materials.

  • Represent Trilogy at DOJ industry days, agency forums, and partner events; shape upcoming acquisitions through pre-RFP customer engagement and capability briefings.

How success is measured:

  • Achievement of annual revenue quota and weighted pipeline coverage targets across the assigned DOJ portfolio.

  • Portfolio gross margin performance against Trilogy Standard BD commission thresholds.

  • Pipeline health and forecast accuracy – qualified opportunities by stage, win rate, and quarter-over-quarter pipeline growth.

  • New DOJ logos and expansion of existing positions through prime and sub-prime contract awards.

What you bring:

We require:

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying federal sales experience, with at least 3 years selling directly to DOJ agencies.

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • Demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding annual revenue targets in the federal market.

  • Deep understanding of DOJ organizational structure, mission priorities, and acquisition processes.

  • Experience working with federal contract vehicles (GSA MAS, GWACs, BPAs) and navigating FAR/DFAR compliance.

  • Strong existing relationships with DOJ decision-makers, program managers, or contracting officers.

  • Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles of 6–18 months.

  • Proficiency with CRM platforms (Salesforce or equivalent) and federal pipeline management.

  • Ability to travel 25–30% of the time to support customer meetings, partner engagements, and industry events.

  • U.S. citizenship required; ability to obtain federal suitability clearance or public trust.

Nice to have:

  • Active security clearance (Secret or higher).

  • Prior experience with law enforcement, justice, or public safety technology solutions.

  • Familiarity with OJP, OVW, NSD, or other DOJ grant-making and regulatory components.

  • Experience with CMMC compliance requirements and FedRAMP-authorized solutions.

Work Environment: Remote with occasional travel as required.

Compensation and Benefits:

Salary range: $120,000 - $135,000 + Trilogy Standard BD Commission

  • Competitive salary based on experience
  • Performance bonus eligibility
  • 401k with company match
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Health Savings Account
  • Professional development programs
  • Employee referral bonus program

Why Trilogy Innovations

At Trilogy Innovations, we believe strong teams build meaningful solutions. We deliver high quality systems and software engineering services across public and private sectors, supporting complex and mission critical environments with integrity, collaboration, and care.

Since 2010, our talented team has partnered with organizations such as the FBI, U.S. Air Force, NASA, Department of Education, Department of Energy, DHS, SOCOM, and leading private sector clients. We are known for combining technical excellence with a thoughtful, people first approach.

At Trilogy, you will work alongside smart, committed professionals in a supportive, learning oriented environment. We value innovation, accountability, and continuous growth, and we encourage our people to bring both expertise and humanity to the work they do.

If you are looking to contribute to impactful work while growing your skills in a collaborative and forward-thinking organization, Trilogy Innovations is a place where you can do just that.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Job Description Summary

The Global Senior Director for Pharma Partnerships is responsible for building, leading, and delivering GE HealthCare’s strategic pharmaceutical alliances to advance both approved and pipeline radiopharmaceutical assets.
This role operates as the enterprise alliance manager for key pharma partnerships, owning senior executive relationships and ensuring delivery of joint strategic, clinical, and commercial objectives. The Director defines partnership strategy, shapes deal constructs, and establishes governance frameworks that enable efficient execution and value realization across the lifecycle.
Working cross-functionally, the leader ensures GE HealthCare assets—including FAPI and the Alzheimer’s disease portfolio—are embedded within pharma development programs, enabling CDx pathways, de-risking development, and ensuring successful global commercialization. The role is central to positioning GE HealthCare as the partner of choice for both pharma and providers. Success in this role is defined by embedding GE HealthCare assets into leading pharma programs, enabling CDx pathways at scale, and consistently delivering partnership value that translates into commercial leadership.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Partnership Strategy & Asset Integration

  • Define and lead the global pharma partnership strategy, aligned to priority assets and disease areas with initial focus on FAPI and AD portfolio
  • Proactively identify and secure opportunities to embed GE HealthCare diagnostics within pharma pipelines and clinical programs
  • Drive early “design-in” of assets to maximize probability of CDx adoption and downstream commercial success
  • Translate partnership insights into portfolio priorities and stage-gate investment decisions
  • Collaborate with CMC, supply chain, regulatory affairs and R&D to build capabilities that enables GEHC to deliver on key pharma partnership priorities

Deal Structuring, Governance & Value Delivery

  • Shape partnership structures, including scope, financial frameworks, milestones, and governance mechanisms
  • Ensure alignment between contractual commitments and operational delivery across all functions
  • Define and track partnership KPIs, ensuring delivery against agreed objectives and value realization
  • Oversee execution of partnership deliverables, including co-development, supply, and commercialization components

Alliance Management & Executive Engagement

  • Serve as the primary alliance manager across strategic pharma partnerships, with end-to-end accountability for outcomes
  • Own C-suite and senior stakeholder relationships, ensuring alignment on strategy, priorities, and value creation
  • Establish and lead Joint Steering Committees and executive governance forums
  • Drive clear escalation pathways, decision rights, and operating cadence to maintain execution velocity

Cross-Functional Integration & Execution

  • Lead cross-functional orchestration across Clinical, Regulatory, Medical, Market Access, Supply, and Commercial teams
  • Align development strategies to enable CDx labeling with efficient clinical and regulatory pathways
  • Coordinate global commercial strategy and launch readiness in alignment with pharma partners
  • Act as the internal integrator to ensure consistency of strategy, messaging, and execution across teams

Risk Management

  • Identify and proactively manage risks across clinical, regulatory, operational, and commercial dimensions
  • Establish structured feedback loops from partnerships to inform future deal-making and asset strategy
  • Drive disciplined, data-based stage-gate decisions based on partnership performance and emerging evidence

External Positioning

  • Reinforce GE HealthCare’s position as a preferred pharma partner through high-quality execution and credibility
  • Build long-term relationships across pharma development, BD, and product leadership teams
  • Expand partnership opportunities across priority assets and disease areas through proactive engagement

Ideal Profile

  • Significant experience in pharmaceutical partnerships, business development, or alliance management, including structuring and executing complex collaborations across development and commercialization
  • Experience shaping partnership strategy and translating it into deal structures, operational plans, and measurable outcomes
  • Strong external credibility, with experience engaging pharma partners, business development leaders, and scientific stakeholders
  • Demonstrated track record of managing strategic partnerships end-to-end, including governance, Joint Steering Committees, and executive-level stakeholder engagement
  • Strong understanding of drug and diagnostic development, with experience supporting or enabling CDx strategies, clinical development programs, and regulatory pathways
  • Proven ability to operate in complex, cross-functional global environments and influence without direct authority across R&D, clinical, regulatory, and commercial teams
  • Experience working across global markets, with appreciation of regional differences in clinical development, regulatory, and market access pathways
  • Track record of influencing C-suite stakeholders and driving alignment across organizations in high-stakes partnerships

GE HealthCare offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, and tuition reimbursement.

With a combination of industry-leading tools, services, and expertise, only Black Duck helps organizations maximize security and quality in DevSecOps and throughout the software development life cycle.

Regional Field Chief Technology Officer

Location: EMEA, Remote (Black Duck has entities in UK, Germany, Netherlands, France, Italy, Ireland, Finland, Sweden)

Black Duck® meets the board-level risks of modern software with True Scale Application Security, ensuring uncompromised trust in software for the regulated, AI-powered world. Only Black Duck solutions free organizations from tradeoffs between speed, accuracy, and compliance at scale while eliminating security, regulatory, and licensing risks. Whether in the cloud or on premises, Black Duck is the only choice for securing mission-critical software everywhere code happens. With Black Duck, security leaders can make smarter decisions and unleash business innovation with confidence.

We are looking for a Regional Field Chief Technology Officer to serve as a senior technical executive, trusted advisor, and public voice of our technology strategy in the market. In this role, the Regional Field CTO will operate at the intersection of technology, sales, and the customer — engaging directly with C-level and technical leaders at our most strategic customer accounts, translating our AI-driven platform capabilities into credible technical narratives, and representing the company as a thought leader across the industry. This is a customer-facing, pre-sales technical leadership role reporting to the VP of Sales Engineering, with a dotted line to Product & Technology.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as trusted technical advisor and recurring executive sponsor for C-level and senior technical stakeholders at strategic, enterprise, federal and other key accounts — pivoting fluidly between business strategy conversations, risk, compliance, and deep technical architecture reviews.
  • Lead highly visible, multidisciplinary technical engagements of strategic importance across the region, including executive briefings, architecture reviews, whiteboard sessions, customer advisory feedback loops, and partner or analyst-facing discussions.
  • Represent Black Duck as a technical evangelist for the platform and roadmap within a region, delivering keynotes, webinars, whitepapers, and thought leadership content at industry events, and representing the company externally with press, analysts, and partners.
  • Translate Black Duck platform AI/ML, detection engine, and platform architecture capabilities into clear, credible narratives for both technical and executive audiences, speaking candidly to responsible AI practices such as data privacy, model governance, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Partner with Sales and Presales leadership on the region’s most strategic and enterprise opportunities, leading technical deep-dives, architecture reviews, whiteboard sessions, and executive briefings, and advising on the technical implications of new product launches, roadmap changes, and competitive positioning.
  • Support RFPs and security questionnaires with authoritative technical input, and articulate competitive and technical differentiation, including nuanced comparisons of AI/ML capabilities against alternatives in the market.
  • Proactively engage strategic accounts to strengthen technical trust, identify expansion opportunities, mitigate renewal risk, and guide customers toward secure software development and application security maturity.
  • Identify and solve problems of strategic or industry scope, using innovative approaches to remove technical barriers, strengthen customer confidence, and improve business outcomes.
  • Provide field-informed guidance on emerging AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, application security trends, and competitive market dynamics that may influence Black Duck strategy or customer adoption.
  • Capture, synthesize, and escalate regional customer, partner, and market feedback into actionable input for Product, Engineering, and Sales systematically capturing technical objections and influencing the roadmap, packaging, launch readiness, and go-to-market strategy.
  • Coach, enable, and review technical storytelling by sales engineers and account executives, including how to explain AI features accurately without overclaiming.

Qualifications and Experience Required:

  • 15+ years in a senior technical leadership role (CTO, Sales Engineering leader, Principal Architect, or equivalent), including several years in a customer-facing or field/pre-sales capacity.
  • Proven track record engaging and influencing C-level and senior technical audiences at enterprise organizations, with demonstrated success across complex enterprise sales cycles.
  • Domain expertise in application security (SAST, SCA, DAST), enterprise architecture, cloud/SaaS platforms, APIs and integrations, and security best practices.
  • Deep, practical understanding of AI/ML concepts as applied to security (e.g., anomaly detection, large language models, behavioral analytics, AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows), along with a candid grasp of their limitations and the practical limitations and controls needed for responsible adoption.
  • Demonstrated success negotiating with and influencing executive leadership, significant customers, partners, analysts, or vendors to shape technical decisions and business outcomes.
  • Ability to exercise wide latitude in determining objectives and approaches for complex, critical assignments with material regional, functional, or market impact.
  • Experience shaping standards, methods, practices, or market-facing technical narratives within an industry or discipline.
  • Proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear stories for both executive and highly technical audiences, including customers, partners, press, analysts, and internal stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated industry presence — conference speaking, published thought leadership, active contribution to industry/analyst communities, customer advisory leadership, or comparable external technical influence.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, able to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and executive audiences.

Company Introduction:

Airspace is a tech-enabled freight forwarder that’s redefining how the world’s most critical packages are delivered. Headquartered in Carlsbad, California, Airspace has employees who are based around the world. Our European headquarters is in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

As a recognized leader in AI and machine learning, our team leverages data and patented technology to coordinate logistics across a global network of drivers and airlines. Our goal is to deliver those packages that are truly mission-critical in a way that is faster, more transparent, more secure, and more accountable than ever before. The items we deliver range from organs for transplant, to parts for critical machinery including grounded aircraft and highly sensitive components such as semiconductors.

Airspace has been rated one of America’s best Startup Employers and listed as one of CNBC’s Disruptor 50 companies. Airspace has the support of leading investors such as Telstra Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Defy Partners, DBL Partners, and Scale Ventures. To date the company has raised more than $140m.

The company is growing rapidly and serving more places around the world than ever before. We are looking for passionate, motivated individuals who want to make an IMPACT every day to help us execute on our mission of reshaping the world of time-critical logistics.

What is the "Dedicated Driver" service?

Airspace partners with leading U.S. Medical Device companies to ensure life-saving equipment is transported safely and securely to hospitals in the local region. If a loved one suffers a serious injury, our Dedicated Drivers are the critical link between warehouses and hospitals, delivering essential surgical tools in real time. Their mission is clear: to equip surgeons with the critical tools for life-saving procedures—because every second counts when a patient is on the table.

About the job:

The Operations Coordinator is the administrative and documentation backbone for the DD Operational Support Team, primarily supporting the Manager of Operational Support, with additional support for Talent Acquisition Specialists and Regional Managers as capacity allows. This role keeps recruiting, onboarding, and training running on schedule by owning scheduling logistics, candidate and training records, and documentation upkeep. It also supports Regional Managers with performance administration, including metrics tracking, coaching documentation, and PIP paperwork. Reporting to the Manager, DD Operational Support, this role sits alongside recruiting and support functions within the DD Operational Support Team.

This is a detail-oriented, process-driven role best suited for someone who is organized, discreet with sensitive information, and comfortable managing recurring documentation and scheduling cycles across multiple stakeholders at once.

As the Dedicated Driver program continues to grow, this role is expected to grow with it. The responsibilities outlined here represent the current scope, and the right candidate should be comfortable taking on new tasks and workflows as the team's needs develop over time.

What you'll do:

  • Coordinate interview scheduling and candidate pipeline logistics, including maintaining and updating candidate records, in partnership with the Talent Acquisition Specialists, keeping candidates moving through the hiring process without delay
  • Support the Talent Acquisition Specialist with candidate interviews as needed, which may include screening calls or sitting in on interview panels
  • Confirm new drivers' account setup and onboarding requirements are fully complete before their start date
  • Help the team track and maintain driver performance metrics and dedicated driver department reports, flagging trends and outliers that warrant attention
  • Monitor shared email queues and route inquiries to the appropriate team member as needed
  • Draft and send mass communications to drivers on an as needed basis such as emails, text blasts, or newsletters
  • Organize documentation storage and confirm naming conventions are followed consistently across recruiting, training, and performance records
  • Monitor live Dedicated Driver orders in real time, checking for order and app milestone accuracy as shipments move through each stage
  • Partner directly with the Talent Acquisition Specialist, Onboarding & Training Manager, and Regional Managers to understand upcoming scheduling and documentation needs, preparing materials in advance of deadlines
  • Escalate documentation gaps, missed deadlines, or inconsistencies to the Manager, DD Operational Support Team
  • Maintain confidentiality and sound judgment when handling sensitive candidate and personnel information
  • Order and coordinate shipment of driver equipment (e.g. uniforms, badges, placards)
  • Support curriculum updates by identifying training gaps and routing them to the training owner for revision
  • Serve as a secondary owner of training/certification tracking, capable of stepping into training program ownership during transitions
  • Take on ad hoc administrative tasks and projects for the broader DD Team as they arise

As the role evolves, additional responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting additional administrative needs as the program and client base expands
  • Assisting with reporting and performance visibility tools for the DD Operational Support team
  • Investigate and resolve weekly driver pay discrepancies, coordinating with Regional Managers and other systems of record as needed
  • Taking on additional Salesforce-based processes as they are developed and documented

Success Metrics

This year: what does success look like in this role this year?

  • Recruiting, onboarding, and training cycles run on schedule with minimal escalations to the Manager, DD Operational Support
  • Candidate and training records are consistently accurate and up to date
  • Performance documentation (coaching notes, performance cases) is complete, filed on time, and audit-ready
  • Order/milestone monitoring catches discrepancies before they affect customer visibility

Next year: what does success look like in this role next year?

  • Demonstrated ownership of a larger or more complex caseload with less oversight
  • Contributing process improvements to scheduling, training tracking, or documentation workflows

Your First 90 Days

  • Learn the DD corporate support team's systems (Salesforce, ATS, LMS) and current documentation workflows
  • Shadow and take over recruiting/onboarding scheduling logistics with the Talent Acquisition Specialist and Onboarding & Training Manager
  • Begin supporting one or more Regional Managers with performance documentation and metrics tracking
  • Build working relationships with key stakeholders (Talent Acquisition Specialist, Onboarding & Training Manager, Regional Managers, Manager of DD Operational Support)

Your First 180 Days

  • Independently manage the full recruiting/onboarding coordination cycle with minimal guidance
  • Own PIP and coaching documentation from initiation through close for assigned Regional Managers
  • Reliably monitor live orders/milestones and flag discrepancies proactively
  • Identify at least one process or documentation improvement to bring to the team

What we're looking for:

  • 1-2+ years of experience in an administrative, coordinator, or operations support role
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when managing schedules, candidate records, and performance data
  • Comfortable working in Salesforce (SFDC), an ATS, or an LMS, or eager to learn; prior experience with any of these is a plus
  • Excellent written communication skills; able to coordinate across multiple stakeholders and summarize data clearly
  • Reliable and self-directed, with a proactive communication style when issues arise
  • Able to work within a remote, cross-timezone team environment
  • Discreet and trustworthy when handling confidential candidate and personnel information
  • Comfortable juggling competing priorities across recruiting, training, and performance support

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Salary Range: $60,000-$65,000/yr + 10% Bonus
  • High-quality health, dental, and vision plan options
  • Open PTO
  • 401K with company match
  • Professional learning and training reimbursements

Core Values:

  • We are One Team. We believe we all accomplish more when we are working together.
  • We make an Impact. We are determined to have a positive influence on our environment, our customers, our industry, and our world.
  • We are Passionate. We care deeply about our mission and are not afraid to raise the bar.
  • We are Transparent. We pride ourselves on having open, honest, and sincere communication with our team and customers.
  • We are Innovative. We never settle and are always striving to improve our product, service, and ourselves.

About the job

Mercor connects elite creative and technical talent with leading AI research labs. Headquartered in San Francisco, our investors include Benchmark, General Catalyst, Peter Thiel, Adam D'Angelo, Larry Summers, and Jack Dorsey.

Position: PDF Annotation & Transcription Experts – Japanese
Type:Contract
Compensation:$34/hour

Role Responsibilities

  • Source documents by finding publicly accessible Japanese PDFs with multimodal elements and record their origins.
  • Annotate structure by identifying and bounding every meaningful region, assigning component types and reading-order indices.

  • Professional experience in interpretation, journalism, transcription, translation, or editorial work.
  • Exact character-level accuracy, prioritizing precision over speed.
  • Systematic approach, applying a taxonomy consistently across documents.
  • Comfort with unfamiliar layouts like vertical text and multi-column newspapers.

Preferred

  • Experience with AI training data annotation, labeling, or bilingual evaluation.
  • Skills in transcription and localization, including MTPE, subtitling, and OCR correction.
  • Document production experience such as typesetting, copy-editing, or proofreading.
  • Knowledge of script and encoding, including Unicode normalization and Japanese input methods.

Hi 👋 I'm Anna, Head of Implementation at Pinpoint.

We're a high-growth, bootstrapped HR tech start-up building and selling software that helps in-house recruitment teams attract, hire, and onboard the right talent. Today, we have a strong foundation in place, with a mature product, rapid growth, strong product-market fit, and happy customers.

You only need to look at our reviews on G2 and Capterra to see how often customers mention the quality of our support and onboarding. That experience starts with implementation.

As we continue to bring on more large, complex customers, we're looking for an Enterprise Implementation Manager to fully own a high volume of mid-market and enterprise implementations from end to end. You'll steer timelines, manage technical complexity, and lead customers confidently through a high-stakes rollout.

The fine print (but way more exciting):
  • This is a remote role based in the UK. Our HQ is in Jersey, UK, and our 100-person team is spread across the UK and US.
  • Initially you'll manage 8–12 active implementations, scaling to 15–20+ as you build efficiency. These are primarily mid-market and enterprise projects, each running an average of 50 days.
  • Our product is deep, flexible, and genuinely complex. You'll work with customers managing intricate, multi-tenant workflows and customizable hiring journeys. You'll need to understand a wide range of customer types, implementation paths, and integration requirements.
  • Pinpoint isn't for everyone. We're still in startup mode: fast-moving, lean, and sometimes ambiguous. You'll thrive here if you're proactive, adaptable, and comfortable building structure where none exists.
  • Our values actually matter here. We hire people who reflect them in how they work, collaborate, and make decisions.

About the Role:

  • Maintain accountability across your implementations, ensuring deadlines are met and blockers are addressed with urgency
  • Own the project management of implementation from kickoff through go-live, tracking milestones, managing risks, and keeping everyone aligned
  • Lead internal and external discovery to understand customer needs and design tailored implementation plans
  • Scope and shepherd HRIS integrations, including reading API docs, mapping data, and reducing engineering dependency where you can
  • Coordinate internal teams across integrations, product, and support to ensure timely delivery and clear communication
  • Act as a trusted advisor to enterprise customers, offering strategic workflow guidance and product best practices
  • Ensure a smooth handover to our Customer Success team post-implementation, while staying involved through early adoption to support long-term success
  • Develop and deliver scalable customer training: live sessions, train-the-trainer programs, and asynchronous enablement materials
Tech stack: Arrows, HubSpot, ClickUp, Slack, Intercom, Linear, Guru

About You:

  • 3+ years leading large-scale B2B SaaS implementations end to end, across multiple different products. Experience with both enterprise and mid-market customers, and HR or recruiting tech is a huge plus
  • Proven experience managing complex, multi-customer B2B SaaS implementations at scale (10+ concurrent), where you balanced competing priorities, internal coordination, and technical complexity across diverse customer needs
  • Technically self-sufficient. Comfortable learning from API documentation, using tools like Postman for troubleshooting, and reducing engineering dependency where possible. You don't need to be a developer, but you're willing to dig in
  • Background in high-growth startup environments (50–250 employees) where you experienced rapid scaling and evolving processes. Bonus if you've worked somewhere that doubled in size during your tenure
  • Structured project owner who builds milestone-driven plans, defines customer responsibilities, and thinks 2 to 3 steps ahead to manage risk
  • Experienced working with global customers and cross-functional teams (product, engineering, CS)
  • Past examples of managing implementation risk: adjusting plans, unblocking tech issues, or driving change
  • Brings operational rigor and accountability to each project. Others trust you to own outcomes, not just tasks
  • AI-forward in how you actually work. You actively use Claude, ChatGPT, or similar tools in your day-to-day—planning, research, communication, training materials. Not a future aspiration; something you're already doing
  • Comfortable working in ambiguous, startup-style environments with evolving processes
  • Professional polish and presence. A clear communicator who can command a (virtual) room
  • Based in the UK

What We Offer:

We want Pinpoint to be the best place you’ve ever worked—somewhere you feel valued, supported, and excited to grow. Here’s what you’ll get:
  • Comprehensive healthcare – Excellent medical, dental, & vision coverage for you and your family
  • Unlimited holidays – Take the time you need to rest and recharge
  • Mental health support – Unlimited, immediate access to professional counseling via Spill
  • Retirement contributions – 401k or pension contributions depending on your location
  • Remote-first – Work where you’re most productive, with flexibility and trust as the default
  • Equity with real upside – Share in the long-term value you help create
  • Fully paid parental leave – Up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents
  • Learning budget – Annual funds for courses, books, or anything that supports your growth
A detailed overview of our benefits can be found here.

raw.description:
THE·TEAM is proud to provide representation and marketing services to talent, brands and properties across 28 countries and more than 70 cities worldwide. Our brands and properties group partners with iconic brands and rights holders to turn relevance into revenue through integrated strategy and consulting, creative, live experiences and commercialization. We help clients understand, connect to and inspire global audiences by bringing together brands, properties and talent/creators to build meaningful relationships that drive measurable business outcomes.


Shaped by our belief in the unifying power of sports, music and entertainment, THE·TEAM leads with intelligence, ideas and influence. For more information, please visit .


Internship Overview
Our internship opportunities within our Brands and Properties division are organized into two primary areas, with sub-specialties available within both.

  • Strategy & Consulting + Experiential: We are strategic advisors, guiding brands and properties to navigate, optimize, and maximize their investments in sports, entertainment, and culture. By blending data-driven intelligence with deep industry expertise, we craft innovative, business-led solutions that drive meaningful impact. Our approach is rooted in strategic foresight, helping our partners not only understand their opportunities but also build, manage, and monetize them effectively. Leveraging our unparalleled industry influence and full suite of services, we bring ideas to life with precision and purpose. From insights + measurement to strategy & planning, management, monetization, hospitality, and experiential activations, we provide end-to-end solutions that elevate partnerships and create lasting value.
  • Creative and Content: THE·TEAM Creative specializes in developing innovative, high-impact storytelling and branding. We craft compelling visual and narrative content, from brand campaigns and social assets to video production and influencer-led marketing. By blending cutting-edge design, digital strategy and cultural insights, we help clients build authentic connections with their audiences, amplifying their presence across multiple platforms. Whether through branded content, influencer collaborations or authentic social experiences, we ensure every piece of content resonates, engages, and drives brand relevance.

What Makes Our Internship Unique
Real work! Our program is designed to introduce aspiring sports and entertainment professionals to the industry and our company by integrating them into client-facing projects that our full-time employees work on every day.

Day-to-day Duties Include:

  • Working with your manager and teams to execute on client work, which varies based on your area of focus, but can include conducting research, assisting on evaluations, ideating on creative development, supporting measurement and ROI analysis, learning the ins and outs of client services, partnering with social influencers and more.
  • Support your discipline as necessary with special projects or tasks that are both short and long term.
  • Partnering with other interns and employees on new business, market research and providing your POV on agency-lead initiatives.

Skills and Qualifications

  • Utilize a fact-based, hypothesis driven approach to problem solving.
  • Demonstrate excellent organizational, time management and communication (written and oral) capabilities.
  • Showcase creative thinking and execution through your work and presentation skills.
  • Express a passion for the sports and / or entertainment industry.

Requirements

  • Students must be able to receive academic credit from their US-based college or university.
  • Open to undergraduate and graduate students

Key Dates:

  • Our Spring 2027 internship application is currently live and set to close on October 9, 2026. Interviews will take place October - November.
  • The Spring internship program starts on January 26, 2027 and ends on April 30, 2027.

Job Description:

GDIT is hiring a Support Assistant to provide help desk support to end users of government information systems, to include Tableau and Salesforce. The Support Assistant works to identify, triage, and resolve or escalate issues.

Position Duties:

  • Provide responsive, consistent, and reliable support to a customer base that provides mission critical support.

  • Provide Tier 1 support for customer support requests and escalate to development and operations teams when appropriate.

  • Perform essential user management tasks such as resolving access issues, processing name changes, and updating email information to facilitate system access.

  • Troubleshoot end user issues across designated platforms, triaging to identified resolver groups as needed.

  • Log all support requests from help desk inquiries into a ticketing system.

  • Work effectively with cross-functional teams to identify and resolve issues.

  • Implement various projects, develop work plans, and ensure timely completion as directed by the IT manager.

  • Assist new and existing users with acquiring access to systems and databases through email support and use of the Service Console.

Qualifications:

  • Requires a BA/BS degree in computer science or related field along with 2+ years of customer support experience in a technical environment.

  • Exceptional customer service skills are required.

  • Strong interpersonal skills for communicating with internal and external personnel of all levels.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Familiarity with Tableau and its functions.

  • Ability to multi-task and work independently with minimal supervision.

  • Ability to keep sensitive information protected.

  • Ability to take direction and remain detail oriented.

Additional Requirements:

  • This position requires an existing T4 Public Trust or the ability to obtain one.

  • This position may require shift hours including weekends and holidays. Shift schedules are based on customer need and are subject to change.

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE

At GDIT, the mission is our purpose, and our people are at the center of everything we do.
● Growth: AI-powered career tool that identifies career steps and learning opportunities
● Support: An internal mobility team focused on helping you achieve your career goals
● Rewards: Comprehensive benefits and wellness packages, 401K with company match, and competitive pay and paid time off
● Flexibility: Full-flex work week to own your priorities at work and at home
● Community: Award-winning culture of innovation and a military-friendly workplace

OWN YOUR OPPORTUNITY
Explore a career at GDIT and you’ll find endless opportunities to grow alongside colleagues who share your ambition to deliver your best work.The likely hourly rate for this position is between $29.52 - $37.95. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. Rather, salary will be set based on experience, geographic location and possibly contractual requirements and could fall outside of this range.

40

Travel Required:

Less than 10%

Remote

Work Location:

USA DC Washington

Additional Work Locations:

Any Location / Remote

Total Rewards at GDIT:

Our benefits package for all US-based employees includes a variety of medical plan options, some with Health Savings Accounts, dental plan options, a vision plan, and a 401(k) plan offering the ability to contribute both pre and post-tax dollars up to the IRS annual limits and receive a company match. To encourage work/life balance, GDIT offers employees full flex work weeks where possible and a variety of paid time off plans, including vacation, sick and personal time, holidays, paid parental, military, bereavement and jury duty leave. GDIT typically provides new employees with 15 days of paid leave per calendar year to be used for vacations, personal business, and illness and an additional 10 paid holidays per year. Paid leave and paid holidays are prorated based on the employee’s date of hire. The GDIT Paid Family Leave program provides a total of up to 160 hours of paid leave in a rolling 12 month period for eligible employees. To ensure our employees are able to protect their income, other offerings such as short and long-term disability benefits, life, accidental death and dismemberment, personal accident, critical illness and business travel and accident insurance are provided or available. We regularly review our Total Rewards package to ensure our offerings are competitive and reflect what our employees have told us they value most.

Our Identify Verification Process:

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during virtual interviews. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. By proceeding, you authorize the collection, processing, and use of your biometric data for identity verification and security purposes.

About our Work:

We are GDIT. A global technology and professional services company that delivers technology solutions and mission services to every major agency across the U.S. government, defense and intelligence community. Our 26,000 experts extract the power of technology to create immediate value and deliver solutions at the edge of innovation. raw.title: Chief Financial Officer
raw.excerpt: Real opportunities.  Real impact.  Your career, redefined.
raw.description:
Real opportunities. Real impact. Your career, redefined.

(NOTE: A human reviews every application at Oceans, so please apply for only one position and only once a year—if you're a better fit for another role, we’ll route your application accordingly and if we’re not quite ready for you, we’ll reach back out later.)

At Oceans, we help the best and brightest of Sri Lanka to take advantage of opportunities that otherwise wouldn’t be available to them, while supporting entrepreneurs around the world. Our community (we call them Divers) don’t do surface work—they go deep to solve complex challenges and make a real impact. And in doing so, they support bold ideas, expand their skills, broaden their expertise, and grow their careers, all without having to leave family and friends.

As the Chief Financial Officer, you will play a critical role in supporting a diversified family office overseeing operating businesses, private equity investments, public equities, and real estate assets. You'll work closely with the principal to build a sophisticated strategic finance capability across the portfolio, providing the forecasting, financial modelling, investment analysis, and quantitative decision support needed to make informed capital allocation decisions.

This role is ideal for a senior finance leader who combines deep FP&A and financial modelling expertise with strong commercial judgment and an investment-oriented mindset. Rather than functioning as a traditional Controller or reporting-focused CFO, you'll act as the principal's senior financial thought partner—building the family's forward-looking finance capability, evaluating investment opportunities, challenging assumptions, identifying risks, and proactively uncovering opportunities to grow and optimize the portfolio.

Here's how you'll make an impact:

Accountability

FP&A, Forecasting & Strategic Planning

  • Build and lead the FP&A function across the family office.
  • Develop integrated forecasts and financial projections across EGE Holdings and its underlying businesses.
  • Build scenario models around operating companies, investments, and portfolio decisions.
  • Establish forward-looking financial planning processes across a previously consolidation-focused finance function.
  • Develop sensitivity analyses to assess potential outcomes under different operating, market, and investment assumptions.
  • Translate forecasts and financial projections into clear recommendations for the principal.
  • Improve visibility into future liquidity, capital requirements, returns, and financial risks.

Investment Analysis & Capital Allocation

  • Serve as the quantitative lead supporting capital allocation decisions across the family office.
  • Evaluate prospective private equity, public market, real estate, and operating-company investments.
  • Build investment, valuation, and return models to assess opportunities and downside scenarios.
  • Perform quantitative risk analysis across existing and prospective investments.
  • Assess trade-offs between competing uses of capital.
  • Develop consistent analytical frameworks for evaluating investment opportunities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve portfolio returns and deploy capital more effectively.
  • Provide objective financial analysis to support significant investment decisions.

Portfolio Risk Analysis

  • Develop a holistic view of financial risk across the family office portfolio.
  • Assess concentration, liquidity, leverage, and investment risks.
  • Model downside and stress scenarios across different asset classes and operating businesses.
  • Evaluate prospective investments in the context of existing portfolio exposure.
  • Identify emerging financial risks and recommend appropriate responses.
  • Provide the principal with clear quantitative insight into risk/reward trade-offs.

Strategic Finance & Decision Support

  • Act as the principal's senior financial thought partner on complex business and investment decisions.
  • Provide quantitative analysis for strategic questions across EGE and its underlying operating companies.
  • Translate financial information into commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Challenge assumptions and provide an independent financial perspective.
  • Identify opportunities to improve profitability, capital efficiency, and portfolio performance.
  • Proactively bring financial insights and opportunities to the principal rather than waiting for requests.
  • Support strategic decisions across new ventures, operating businesses, and investment activities.

Consolidated Financial Management

  • Own consolidated financial reporting across EGE Holdings and its underlying entities.
  • Ensure the principal has clear visibility into financial performance across the ownership structure.
  • Oversee entity-level financial reporting and consolidation.
  • Coordinate multi-entity tax requirements with external tax advisors.
  • Establish financial reporting standards that provide decision-useful insight beyond statutory and tax requirements.
  • Maintain appropriate financial controls and reporting standards across the portfolio.

Finance Leadership & Controller Management

  • Lead and develop controllers and finance leaders embedded within EGE's operating companies.
  • Establish consistent standards and expectations across entity-level finance functions.
  • Review the quality and usefulness of financial reporting produced across the portfolio.
  • Coach controllers toward stronger analytical and commercially focused finance capabilities.
  • Create greater connectivity between operating-company finance and family-office decision-making.
  • Build a scalable finance organization as EGE's portfolio grows.
  • Identify gaps in finance capabilities and determine where additional resources are required.

External Advisor & Financial Partner Management

  • Partner effectively with private banks, wealth advisors, tax professionals, legal counsel, and other external financial stakeholders.
  • Review and challenge external financial analysis where appropriate.
  • Determine which analytical capabilities should be developed and maintained internally.
  • Reduce unnecessary dependence on external advisors by strengthening internal financial capabilities.
  • Maintain productive external relationships while retaining internal ownership of financial analysis and decision-making.

AI-Enabled Finance

  • Use AI tools to accelerate financial analysis, research, modelling, reporting, and decision support.
  • Leverage Claude and other advanced AI tools within day-to-day finance workflows.
  • Identify opportunities to automate or improve recurring financial analysis and reporting.
  • Apply appropriate financial judgment and validation to AI-assisted outputs.
  • Help establish efficient, AI-enabled workflows across the broader finance organization.

Colleagues

You'll work closely with the principal, controllers and finance leaders across EGE's operating companies, private banks, wealth advisors, tax professionals, legal counsel, and other external financial partners. As the senior financial owner of the family office, you'll connect portfolio-level financial information with strategic decision-making and ensure the principal has the insight needed to allocate capital effectively.

At Oceans Talent, you'll also receive guidance and support from your Operations Manager, who will help you succeed in the role and ensure that you're continuously growing and developing in your career.

Skills and Qualifications

As a Chief Financial Officer, your vertical focus will be on strategic finance, FP&A, financial modelling, investment analysis, and capital allocation, while your horizontal focus will include portfolio risk, consolidated reporting, finance leadership, stakeholder management, and AI-enabled financial analysis.

  • Experience: Significant senior-level finance leadership experience, ideally as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of FP&A, Investment Finance leader, or equivalent strategic finance role within a sophisticated investment or multi-entity environment.
  • FP&A: Deep experience building and leading forecasting, planning, projection, and scenario-modelling capabilities.

  • Strategic Financial Leadership: Your ability to develop and lead financial strategy in alignment with broader business objectives and long-term growth plans.

Diversity of experience is core to Oceans. You are expected to work inclusively with individuals from a variety of backgrounds, ensuring that both personal and collective dignity are supported.

Job Description:

ITW (Illinois Tool Works) is a Fortune 300 global manufacturer with approximately 44,000 employees across 51 countries. For over 100 years, we’ve delivered innovative, customer-focused solutions in industries ranging from automotive and aerospace to construction and electronics.

Our success is driven by our differentiated business model comprised of our unique core capabilities: our 80/20 approach, customer-back innovation, and our decentralized, entrepreneurial culture. These capabilities are unmistakably ITW and key to our longevity and strong performance. Our products and solutions are at work all over the world, and we are never more than a few steps from an innovative ITW solution.

ITW Commercial Construction North America (CCNA), a division of ITW, includes trusted brands like Buildex® (Teks®, Sammys®), Red Head (TruBolt®, Tapcon®), Ramset (Trakfast®), and PNA®, serving professional contractors since 1910. We design and manufacture innovative fastening, and concrete flatwork solutions for concrete, drywall, metal buildings, fire protection, plumbing, electrical, and HVAC applications.

We’re committed to operational excellence, responsive service, and continuous product innovation, and are always focused on meeting the evolving needs of the commercial construction industry.

We are currently looking for a Field Sales Engineer to join our team! This individual will identify and engage with top building owners, architectural, engineering, general contractor, and design firms targeted within chosen metro markets with the goal of adding CCNA products on the master specification and driving sales of specified products. This is a remote role, with preference for candidates to be located in major markets within the Eastern United States.

Primary responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with key architectural, engineering, and design firms to influence product specifications and drive specification conversions.
  • Create, recommend, and execute specification programs across targeted markets to achieve annual conversion and growth objectives.
  • Provide technical training, product application guidance, and code-related support to architects, engineers, designers, building owners, and Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs).
  • Analyze market trends, competitive activity, and customer insights to identify opportunities and drive specification growth strategies.
  • Support the sales team by providing technical expertise, interpreting engineering reports and building codes, and demonstrating design equivalency for key projects.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Engineering, and other cross-functional teams to develop and execute specification selling plans while providing Voice of Customer insights to support the CBI pipeline.
  • Measure program effectiveness, monitor results, and provide recommendations for continuous improvement and business growth.

Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering required; Master's degree preferred.
  • 3+ years of technical sales or specification-selling experience; PE license or progress toward licensure preferred.
  • Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to effectively influence multiple decision-makers.
  • Ability to read construction drawings, analyze project specifications, and interpret building code requirements.
  • Results-oriented with strong organizational skills, the ability to manage multiple priorities, and excellent follow-through.

The pay range for this position is $100,000 to $110,000. Base pay within this range is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to geographic location, relevant skills, experience, and education This position is eligible to participate in an annual incentive plan/sales incentive plan.

In addition to a competitive salary, employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance; disability and life insurance; a 401(k) plan with company match and additional employer contributions; flexible spending accounts. raw.description:
About Us

At Sureify we’re helping a large and critical industry -- life insurance -- modernize and innovate. We have built a platform, enabling a core suite of digital solutions for some of the world’s leading insurance companies. We’re passionate about enhancing customer experiences and driving growth through cutting-edge technology.

Position Summary

We are seeking a client-facing Technical Solution Lead to join our Professional Services organization. This role serves as the day-to-day technical solution owner for enterprise SaaS implementations, partnering closely with clients to translate business objectives into implementation-ready solutions.

The Technical Solution Lead works alongside a Project Delivery Lead and is supported by Senior Architects, Business Analysts, and Technical Business Analysts. While Senior Architects provide architectural governance and make complex design decisions, the Technical Solution Lead owns the day-to-day technical solutioning effort throughout the implementation lifecycle.

This role is ideal for someone with strong technical analysis and client-facing consulting skills who aspires to become a Solution Architect.

What You'll Do

Client Solution Leadership

  • Serve as the primary, day-to-day technical leader for a client implementation. This role is dedicated to one client at a time, allowing you to focus 100%.
  • Facilitate technical discovery and solution design working sessions with client stakeholders.
  • Partner with the client's architects, business analysts, and technology teams to define implementation approaches. You'll be able to collaborate with a Sureify Senior Architect as needed.
  • Review and approve agile stories produced by Business Analysts and Technical Business Analysts to ensure business requirements are accurately translated for the engineering team.

Solution Design & Analysis

  • Decompose business requirements into implementation-ready user stories.
  • Define API integrations, data mappings, validation rules, and business processes.
  • Identify technical risks, assumptions, and dependencies early in the project lifecycle.
  • Produce high-quality solution documentation and implementation guidance.

Delivery Partnership

  • Partner closely with the Project Delivery Lead to ensure solution readiness throughout delivery.
  • Collaborate with Business Analysts and Technical Business Analysts to refine requirements.
  • Support engineering teams by clarifying functional and technical requirements.
  • Escalate complex architectural decisions to Senior Architects while independently driving day-to-day solution definition.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

  • Leverage consistent solution design standards for your implementation by consulting with Senior Architects on patterns established at other clients.
  • Leverage AI-assisted tools to improve documentation, requirements decomposition, and solution quality.
  • Contribute to Sureify’s best practices in the form of lessons learned and reusable delivery assets.

Required Qualifications

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • 4–6 years of experience in enterprise software implementation, solution consulting, technical business analysis, or solution architecture.
  • Experience working with enterprise SaaS platforms.
  • Strong understanding of REST APIs, JSON, data integration, and SQL.
  • Experience translating business requirements into technical solutions.
  • Comfortable with facilitating working sessions with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Experience working directly with software engineering teams.
  • Exposure to cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure.
  • Experience working in Agile software delivery environments.
  • Bachelor's degree.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in the Life & Annuity insurance industry.
  • Experience working in Fintech, Insurtech, technology consulting, or at an insurance carrier or financial services firm.
  • Familiarity with policy administration systems, identity providers, data middleware, and digital servicing portals.
  • Experience using AI tools to improve solution design or delivery processes.

Success in This Role

Within your first year, you will:

  • Be the day-to-day technical leader for a major new enterprise client.
  • Build trusted relationships with the client's technical and program management staff.
  • Produce implementation-ready solution designs with minimal oversight.
  • Partner with a Senior Architect to focus on architectural governance and complex technical decisions.
  • Improve delivery quality through better requirements decomposition and solution clarity.
  • Help scale our delivery organization through consistent, repeatable leadership.

What Makes This Role Unique

Unlike a traditional Business Analyst or Solution Architect, the Technical Solution Lead owns the day-to-day technical solutioning effort throughout an implementation.

You will spend much of your time collaborating directly with clients—leading working sessions, solving technical challenges, defining APIs and client-side integrations, overseeing data mappings, and ensuring our engineering teams have everything they need to build successfully.

If you enjoy solving complex business problems, working closely with customers, and aspire to become a Solution Architect, this role provides an exceptional career path.

Base annual salary
$135,000—$170,000 USD

Our Guiding Principles

Our products are for nothing if their creators are not fulfilled in their work. We want our employees to flourish at Sureify. We do not fawn over status or titles, instead, we honor effort and intelligence. The best idea wins no matter which colleague proposed it. We do not shortcut our mission with overblown claims or false promises. Sticking to the truth is both a strategy and a principle for us.

Sureify is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, age, disability, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

If you are a California resident, please be aware Sureify collects personal information from you during the application process, which may include your name, contact details, employment history, and educational background, in accordance with the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). We use this information solely to evaluate your candidacy for employment and may share it with internal hiring personnel as needed.
